In the phrase "a sense of 'collective ownership'" (Paragraph 4), the adjective "collective" describes the quality or nature of the ownership, indicating that it is shared among members of a group.

a) Incorrect - demonstrative adjectives point out specific nouns (this, that, these, those), which "collective" does not do.

b) Incorrect - quantitative adjectives indicate number or amount, which is not implied here.

c) Correct - "collective" describes the inherent quality of the noun "ownership" (Paragraph 4).

d) Incorrect - distributive adjectives refer to individual members separately (each, every), which is not the case here.

Hence, option (c) is correct.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. By the time the sun sets, we ______ the summit of the mountain.
questions.questionHtml:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

By the time the sun sets, we ______ the summit of the mountain.
questions.solution:
The most appropriate option to fill in the blank is 'will have reached'. "Will have reached" is the future perfect tense. The future perfect tense is used to emphasise the completion of an action before another future event or time. In the given sentence, it indicates that the action of reaching the summit of the mountain will be completed before a specified future time (by the time the sun sets).

Option (a) is not correct because it uses an incorrect verb form for the future perfect tense. When forming the future perfect tense, the verb "have" is followed by the past participle form of the main verb. The past participle form of "reach" is "reached." Therefore, the correct form of the verb should be "will have reached" instead of "will have reaching."

Option (b) is incomplete and grammatically incorrect. It lacks a helping verb such as "will" to form a complete verb phrase. Additionally, the present participle "reaching" on its own does not convey the future perfect tense required in the sentence.

Option (c) is incorrect because it does not use the correct structure for forming the future perfect tense. The future perfect tense is formed with the auxiliary verb "will have" followed by the past participle form of the main verb.

Complete sentence: By the time the sun sets, we will have reached the summit of the mountain.

Hence, (d) is the correct answer.

Note:

Participle: A word formed from a verb (e.g. going, gone, being, been) and used as an adjective (e.g. working woman, burnt toast) or a noun (e.g. good breeding). In English, participles are also used to make compound verb forms (e.g. is going, has been). Consider the sentences given below:

Dancing at the party, the women fell on the ground.

Encouraged by her parents, Rita went on to pursue her passion.

The highlighted word in the first sentence is of the form Verb + ing and is used as a present participle. It is used to denote an action that is going on or incomplete or imperfect.

The highlighted word in the second sentence is of the form verb + ed. It is used as a past participle. It denotes the completed action or state of the thing spoken of.

A past participle ends with the following: -ed, -d, -t, -en, or -n.

One should take great care and never get confused between a gerund and a present participle. They use the same forms but perform different functions: a gerund is a verbal noun, while a present participle is a verbal adjective.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. You enjoy playing video games, _________?
questions.questionHtml:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

You enjoy playing video games, _________?
questions.solution:
The correct option to fill in the blank is 'don't you'. When the main sentence/clause is positive, the question tag should be negative, and vice versa. In the given case, the main sentence/clause is positive. Therefore, the question tag should be negative. Also, if the main clause lacks an auxiliary verb (be, have etc.), a suitable form of "do" (does, do, did) is introduced in the question tag. Accordingly, option (b) is the correct choice as it maintains the opposite polarity (positive main sentence, negative question tag) and uses the appropriate form of 'do.'

Options (a) and (c) are not correct as they do not adhere to the grammatical rules. In the given sentence, there is no auxiliary verb. Accordingly, a suitable form of 'do' (does, do, did) should be used (not aren't or hasn't).

Option (d) is also not correct because it does not adhere to the grammatical rule that a positive main clause should have a negative question tag ('do you' is again positive).

Hence, (b) is the correct answer.

The complete sentence is: "You enjoy playing video games, don't you?"

NOTE:

Auxiliary verb: A verb that gives grammatical information that is not given by the main verb of a sentence. It supports the main verb. Auxiliary verbs help to form the various tenses, moods, and voices of other verbs. The principal ones are be, do, and have. Example: She will sing a song tomorrow. Here, 'will' is the auxiliary verb that supports the main verb 'sing'.

"Clause: A clause is a group of words that contains a verb (and usually other components too). A clause may form part of a sentence, or it may be a complete sentence in itself. Example:

I. "His products weren't selling"; this is an example of a sentence containing one clause.

II. "After we had had dinner, we went for a walk"; here, the sentence contains two clauses that are separated by a comma.

A clause can be categorised as:

I. Main/independent clause

II. Subordinate/dependent clause

Main/independent clause: In the example 2 given above, the clause "we went for a walk" can be said as the main clause (a clause that is not dependent on any other clause for its meaning, it makes sense on its own; a sentence contains at least one main clause.)

Subordinate/dependent clause: In example 2 given above, the clause "After we had had dinner" is a subordinate clause: it depends on the main clause for its meaning and cannot exist as a sentence on its own.

questions.question: The following sentence has been divided into parts. One of them may contain an error. Select the part that contains the error from the given options. The team have/ won the championship/ for the third year/ in a row.

questions.solution:
The part that contains the error is 'the team have'. The error is related to subject-verb agreement. The subject "the team" is a collective noun that refers to a single unit, so it takes a singular verb form. But the verb 'have' is used with plural subjects, not singular subjects (the team). Accordingly, we need to use the singular 'has' with the singular subject 'the team'. Hence, (d) is the correct answer.

The correct sentence is: The team has won the championship for the third year in a row.

NOTE:

Subject-verb agreement means that a subject and its verb must be both singular or both plural:

A singular subject takes a singular verb.

A plural subject takes a plural verb.

For example, in the sentence 'John lives in France', the subject John (singular 'he') 'agrees with' the third person singular form of the verb to live - lives.
